# Devices: choosing and connecting components

<!-- Generated by scripts/device_docs.py. Edit component docstrings, not this file. -->

These explanations and executable examples come directly from the device code. The [photonic notebook walkthrough](../examples/device_guide.md) is generated from the same docstrings.

Register component classes or compiled subcircuit objects in `compile_circuit`'s model mapping. Wire their documented external ports; internal states are solver unknowns. Netlist builders return topology dictionaries instead. See [Writing components](../writing_components.md) for authoring instructions.

Optical circuits use complex envelopes; use `is_complex=True` and enable float64. At z0=1 a matched incident field has power `abs(a)**2` W. Under reflection, total node voltage is not the incident field. See the [shared conventions](photonic_conventions.md). For mixed-domain small signals use explicit I/Q [quadrature response](photonics.md#running-examples-and-small-signal-response).

## Electronic / Basic elements

### `Capacitor`

Two-terminal stored charge Q=C*(V1-V2).

Connect p1/p2; C is in farads. The same charge law supplies AC and transient dynamics.

[Detailed model reference](index.md) · [API and source](../references/components/electronic.md#circulax.components.electronic.Capacitor)

```python
from circulax.components.electronic import Capacitor

f, q = Capacitor(C=1e-12)(p1=2.0, p2=0.0)
assert abs(q["p1"] - 2e-12) < 1e-24
assert q["p1"] + q["p2"] == 0
print("Stored terminal charge:", q["p1"], "C")
```

### `Inductor`

Two-terminal inductive branch. L is in henries; its branch current is an internal solved state.

[Detailed model reference](index.md) · [API and source](../references/components/electronic.md#circulax.components.electronic.Inductor)

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np

from circulax.components.electronic import Inductor

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
model = Inductor()
# Constitutive F/Q evaluation; physical circuit boundaries are shown in the model reference.
y = jnp.zeros(len(model.ports) + len(model.states), dtype=jnp.float64)
f, q = model.solver_call(0.0, y, model)
assert np.isfinite(f).all()
assert np.isfinite(q).all()
print(Inductor.__name__, "ports:", model.ports)
```

### `Resistor`

Ohmic two-terminal resistor. Connect p1/p2; R is in ohms and current into p1 is (V1-V2)/R.

[Detailed model reference](index.md) · [API and source](../references/components/electronic.md#circulax.components.electronic.Resistor)

```python
from circulax.components.electronic import Resistor

f, q = Resistor(R=100.0)(p1=1.0, p2=0.0)
assert abs(f["p1"] - 0.01) < 1e-12
assert f["p1"] + f["p2"] == 0
print("Current at 1 V:", f["p1"], "A")
```

### `BJT_PNP`

PNP Ebers–Moll transistor, the polarity complement of ``BJT_NPN``.

Currents are positive entering the named terminals. Parameters retain the
positive magnitudes and units of the NPN model. Use ``BJT_PNP_Dynamic`` for
depletion and diffusion charge. The same junction-voltage clipping as the
NPN reference applies.

PNP conduction; dynamic variant adds terminal storage.

### `BJT_PNP_Dynamic`

PNP Ebers–Moll transistor with conservative terminal charges.

Parameters match ``BJT_NPN_Dynamic``: ``Is`` in A, ``Vt/Vje/Vjc`` in V,
``Cje/Cjc`` in F, ``Tf/Tr`` in s, and dimensionless gains and grading
coefficients. Both currents and charges obey ``PNP(v) = -NPN(-v)``.
Consequently DC, AC and transient behavior use a single set of NPN physics
equations; all inherited numerical limits also apply.

PNP conduction; dynamic variant adds terminal storage.

[Detailed model reference](pnp.md) · [API and source](../references/components/bipolar.md#circulax.components.bipolar.BJT_PNP_Dynamic)

### `Comparator`

Finite-response comparator with state-based positive-feedback hysteresis.

``Tau * dx/dt = tanh((Vin_p - Vin_m - Vth + Vh*x)/Vsmooth) - x``.
The bounded normalized state x drives a floating Thevenin output between
Vlow and Vhigh relative to out_m. Tau is seconds, Rout is ohms, other
parameters are volts. Require Tau/Rout/Vsmooth > 0, Vh >= 0 and Vhigh > Vlow.

Hysteresis is bistable when Vh > Vsmooth. The quasi-static thresholds are
Vth +/- (Vh*z - Vsmooth*atanh(z)), z=sqrt(1-Vsmooth/Vh). Vh therefore
approaches the half hysteresis width as Vsmooth becomes small. Select a
stable initial branch through x or a prior unambiguous input bias; there
is no hidden Python state. Inputs have infinite impedance. Supply loading,
common-mode limits and stochastic switching are not modeled.

Finite response and dynamic hysteresis.

[Detailed model reference](comparator.md) · [API and source](../references/components/comparator.md#circulax.components.comparator.Comparator)

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np

from circulax.components.comparator import Comparator

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
model = Comparator()
# Constitutive F/Q evaluation; physical circuit boundaries are shown in the model reference.
y = jnp.zeros(len(model.ports) + len(model.states), dtype=jnp.float64)
f, q = model.solver_call(0.0, y, model)
assert np.isfinite(f).all()
assert np.isfinite(q).all()
print(Comparator.__name__, "ports:", model.ports)
```

### `OpAmp`

Dominant-pole op-amp with finite output resistance, rails and slew rate.

``A`` is dimensionless DC open-loop gain, ``GBW`` the gain-bandwidth
product in Hz, ``Rout`` output resistance in ohms, ``SR`` slew rate in
V/s, and ``RailTau`` output limiting response in seconds. ``Vmin/Vmax``
bound the differential internal driver voltage relative to ``out_m``.
Require positive A/GBW/Rout/SR/RailTau and Vmin < Vmax.

A dynamic rail constraint limits outward motion of the driver state,
avoiding saturation windup. Inputs have infinite impedance; the output
is a floating Thevenin driver. Explicit rail settings do not model supply
loading or common-mode limits. Reactive loads can briefly pull terminal
voltage beyond the internal driver rails through Rout.

Finite gain/bandwidth, output resistance, slew and rail limits.

[Detailed model reference](opamp.md) · [API and source](../references/components/opamp.md#circulax.components.opamp.OpAmp)

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np

from circulax.components.opamp import OpAmp

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)

# Constitutive F/Q evaluation; physical circuit boundaries are shown in the model reference.

f, q = model.solver_call(0.0, y, model)
assert np.isfinite(f).all()
assert np.isfinite(q).all()
print(OpAmp.__name__, "ports:", model.ports)
```

### `PMOSDynamic`

PMOS polarity complement of the generic square-law ``NMOSDynamic``.

``Vth`` defaults to -1 V; its magnitude is passed to the NMOS model.
``Kp`` is A/V², W/L are m, ``lam`` is 1/V, ``Cox`` is F/m², and the
two overlap coefficients are F. Currents are positive into terminals.
Both currents and stored charge obey PMOS(v) = -NMOS(-v). This gives
positive overlap capacitances for nonnegative overlap coefficients.

The same piecewise Meyer charge model and its region-boundary
discontinuities as ``NMOSDynamic`` apply. No bulk terminal, junctions,
subthreshold conduction or charge-recovery states are included.

Generic PMOS conduction with intrinsic/overlap charge.

[Detailed model reference](pmos_dynamic.md) · [API and source](../references/components/mosfet.md#circulax.components.mosfet.PMOSDynamic)

```python

import jax.numpy as jnp
```

### `R2ETCMC`

Nonlinear resistor and explicit electrothermal composition.

**Validation reference:** Verilog-A/OSDI comparisons use the same pinned
[upstream source](https://github.com/dwarning/VA-Models/blob/6099b4e12e6f66ff530f59b8d01fb909094be85a/code/r3_cmc/vacode/r3_cmc.va),
with comparison cases in `tests/test_r3.py`.
These are implementation/parity checks, not measured-device calibration.
Live comparisons require optional compiler/OSDI tools; stored fixtures are
used where provided. Test coverage and adaptations are described in the model reference.
For the documented full-pinch-off cases, reference derivatives use finite
differences of the OSDI residual because its analytic Jacobian disagrees.

[Detailed model reference](r3.md) · [API and source](../references/components/r3.md#circulax.components.r3.R3_CMC)

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np

from circulax.components.r3 import R3_CMC

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
model = R3_CMC()
# Constitutive F/Q evaluation; physical circuit boundaries are shown in the model reference.
y = jnp.zeros(len(model.ports) + len(model.states), dtype=jnp.float64)
f, q = model.solver_call(0.0, y, model)
assert np.isfinite(f).all()
assert np.isfinite(q).all()
print(R3_CMC.__name__, "ports:", model.ports)
```

### `r2_thermal_subcircuit`

Return a recursive-netlist body with an explicit thermal R/C network.

Register model names ``R2ETCMC``, ``Resistor`` and ``Capacitor`` when
compiling. Ports are ``n1``, ``n2`` and ``dt`` (temperature rise in K).
Thermal resistance is K/W and capacitance is J/K. The built-in thermal
network is replaced, so geometry-dependent thermal parameters supplied
in ``resistor_settings`` are overridden by the explicit R/C values.

Nonlinear resistor and explicit electrothermal composition.

[Detailed model reference](r2.md) · [API and source](../references/components/r2.md#circulax.components.r2.r2_thermal_subcircuit)

```python
from circulax.components.r2 import r2_thermal_subcircuit

netlist = r2_thermal_subcircuit(thermal_resistance=1e3, thermal_capacitance=1e-6)
assert {"core", "Rth", "Cth"} <= netlist["instances"].keys()
# Register R2ETCMC, Resistor and Capacitor in the parent model mapping.
print("Thermal subcircuit ports:", tuple(netlist["ports"]))
```

## Photonic / Electrical and thermal phase control

### `ElectricalPhaseShifter`

Ideal control-only reciprocal phase shifter (efficiency rad/V).

No electrical loading or propagation delay. loss_per_v2 is nonnegative
excess power attenuation in dB/V² about bias, with baseline loss_dB.
The real control voltage affects both optical quadratures.

Voltage-controlled phase (`efficiency` in rad/V) and optional voltage-dependent loss.

[Detailed model reference](phase_shifters.md) · [API and source](../references/components/phase_shifters.md#circulax.components.phase_shifters.ElectricalPhaseShifter)

### `JouleHeater`

Ohmic heater; resistance is specified at ambient temperature in kelvin.

``alpha`` is fractional resistance change per K. Physical heat uses the
real drive voltage, while full complex conduction restores imaginary
electrical voltages. The imaginary thermal term constrains the auxiliary
complex representation and injects no physical heat.

Ohmic electrical conduction and local Joule heat, optionally with resistance versus temperature.

[Detailed model reference](thermo_optic.md) · [API and source](../references/components/thermo_optic.md#circulax.components.thermo_optic.JouleHeater)

```python
import numpy as np

from circulax.components.thermo_optic import JouleHeater

f, q = JouleHeater(resistance=100.0)(hp=1.0, hn=0.0, dt=0.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(f["hp"], 0.01)
np.testing.assert_allclose(-f["dt"], 0.01)
print("Heater current: 10 mA; generated heat: 10 mW")
```

The capacitance is constant and the optical flight delay is bidirectional.

### `ThermalPhaseShifter`

Matched reciprocal optical core with phase efficiency in rad/K.

Positive phase multiplies the field by exp(+i*phase). Incident internal
states are pseudo-voltages; their power is |a|²/z0. There is no propagation
delay or optical absorption heating. The dt port must connect to a thermal
network or prescribed temperature-rise boundary.

Optical phase controlled by local temperature, with efficiency in rad/K.

[Detailed model reference](thermo_optic.md) · [API and source](../references/components/thermo_optic.md#circulax.components.thermo_optic.ThermalPhaseShifter)

### `thermo_optic_phase_shifter`

Return a reusable Circuit with heater, optical core and thermal R/C.

Ports are hp, hn, o1, o2, dt and thermal_reference. The exposed dt measurement/control node is
allocated explicitly. Ground thermal_reference to define zero temperature
rise at ambient. Positive Rth/Cth are required for the claimed dynamics.
Parameters are setup constants; the flattened heater/optical/Rth/Cth instance
parameters can subsequently be updated through the ordinary Circuit API.

## Photonic / Interferometers and modulators

### `lumped_mzm`

Compile couplers and loaded phase arms with an ideal transformer drive.

Drive voltage p-n creates arm voltages +V/2,-V/2 (push-pull) or V,0.
Each arm retains its series R and shunt C, so its optical control has an RC
response. The lossless drive transformer reflects arm currents into p-n, preserving
finite input loading and the work delivered to each RC arm.

A Mach–Zehnder with finite RC-loaded phase arms and single-arm or push-pull drive.

[Detailed model reference](modulators.md) · [API and source](../references/components/modulators.md#circulax.components.modulators.lumped_mzm)

```python
import jax
import numpy as np

from circulax import attach_testbench, compile_circuit
from circulax.components import OpticalCW, lumped_mzm
from circulax.components.electronic import Resistor, VoltageSource

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
device = lumped_mzm(efficiency=0.7, resistance=100.0, capacitance=1e-12)
net = {
    "instances": {"MZM": {"component": "mzm"}},
    "ports": {p: f"MZM,{p}" for p in ("in", "in_aux", "out", "out_aux", "p", "n")},
}
net = attach_testbench(
    net,
    sources={
        "in": {"name": "LIGHT", "component": "light", "settings": {"power": 0.002}},
        "p": {"name": "DRIVE", "component": "voltage", "settings": {"V": 0.2}},
    },
    loads={
        p: {"name": name, "component": "resistor", "settings": {"R": 1.0}}
        for p, name in (("in_aux", "DUMP_IN"), ("out", "LOAD"), ("out_aux", "DUMP_OUT"))
    },
    gnd=["n"],
)
circuit = compile_circuit(
    net,
    {"mzm": device, "light": OpticalCW, "voltage": VoltageSource, "resistor": Resistor},
    is_complex=True,
)
field = complex(circuit.port(circuit.dc(), "LOAD,p1"))
np.testing.assert_allclose(abs(field) ** 2, 0.002 * (1 + np.sin(0.7 * 0.2)) / 2, atol=1e-10)
print("Loaded MZM output power:", abs(field) ** 2, "W")
```

### `mach_zehnder`

Compile reciprocal four-optical-port MZI with two genuine couplers.

Both complementary outputs are exposed. Arms have independent +phase
and power insertion loss; interference preserves the coherent output phase.

Two couplers and two independently phased/lossy arms.

[Detailed model reference](modulators.md) · [API and source](../references/components/modulators.md#circulax.components.modulators.mach_zehnder)

```python

device = mach_zehnder()

```

### `traveling_wave_mzm`

Compile the tutorial modal-electrode MZM; no source/termination added.

Supply fitted RLGCTransmissionLine objects (mode_transmission_line).
Each cell uses two half-line ladders, a differential adapter and two real
RC-loaded delayed PN arms. n_sections controls spatial resolution.

A distributed electrode coupled to delayed loaded PN sections.

[Detailed model reference](modulators.md) · [API and source](../references/components/modulators.md#circulax.components.modulators.traveling_wave_mzm)

```python
import numpy as np

from circulax.components.modulators import traveling_wave_mzm
from circulax.components.transmission_line import mode_transmission_line

frequencies = np.r_[0.0, np.geomspace(1e6, 20e9, 20)]
line = mode_transmission_line(frequencies, attenuation_db_per_m=200.0, n_eff=2.2, impedance=55.0)
device = traveling_wave_mzm(differential_line=line, common_line=line, n_sections=1)
assert {"optical_in", "optical_out", "d_in", "d_out", "c_in", "c_out"} <= set(device.ports)
print("Distributed sections: 1; complex unknowns:", device.sys_size)
```

## Photonic / Optical sources and propagation

### `NonlinearOpticalWaveguide`

Promoted bidirectional delayed waveguide with linear loss and TPA.

From examples/photonic/photonics_transient.ipynb. ``a1/a2`` retain the
notebook's incident pseudo-voltage convention: incident power = |a|²/z0.
``tpa_coeff`` is in 1/(W cm). Counterpropagating beams are attenuated
independently (no cross-TPA, Kerr, carrier or thermal coupling).
Nonnegative length/loss/TPA and group index, positive wavelength/z0 required.
Carrier propagation exp(-i beta L) and group delay are each applied once.

Bidirectional delayed waveguide with independent directional two-photon absorption. Length is in um and linear
loss in dB/cm. No cross-TPA, Kerr or carrier-heating physics.

### `OpticalDelayLine`

Waveguide modelled as an explicit time-of-flight delay line (real group delay).

Unlike :func:`OpticalWaveguide` -- which is a steady-state S-matrix stamp
with no envelope flight time -- this component enforces
the actual transient envelope delay: the output field at ``p2`` is the
input field at ``p1`` from ``tau = length_um * n_group / c`` seconds ago,
attenuated and phase-shifted, via a VCVS-style constraint (same pattern as
:func:`TunableBeamSplitter`). ``p1`` carries no self-stamp and must be
driven by a connected source/component, matching that same convention.

See ``circulax.solvers.assembly`` for how the delayed local state is
computed -- a fixed-size accepted-step history buffer read via
``jnp.interp``, vmapped per-instance since ``tau`` may vary across
instances of different length. Adaptive and fixed step-size controllers
may take steps longer than ``tau``; interpolation against the current
Newton trial supplies the required delay Jacobian in that regime.

Args:
    signals: Current and delayed component-local fields and branch state.
    length_um: Waveguide length in micrometres. Defaults to ``100.0``.
    loss_dB_cm: Propagation loss in dB/cm. Defaults to ``1.0``.
    neff: Effective refractive index, used for the carrier phase shift
        over the delay. Defaults to ``2.4``.
    n_group: Group refractive index; sets the propagation delay via
        ``tau = length_um * n_group / c``. Defaults to ``4.0``.
    wavelength_nm: Operating wavelength in nm. Defaults to ``1310.0``.

A directed, buffered envelope delay used by existing examples.

[Detailed model reference](photonic_conventions.md) · [API and source](../references/components/photonic.md#circulax.components.photonic.OpticalDelayLine)

```python

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np

assert np.isfinite(q).all()
```

### `OpticalSource`

Ideal CW optical source for DC and small-signal AC analysis.

Enforces a fixed complex field amplitude ``sqrt(power) * exp(j * phase)``

    phase: Output field phase in radians. Defaults to ``0.0``.

### `OpticalSourcePulse`

Time-dependent optical source with a sigmoid turn-on profile.

Field amplitude ramps smoothly from zero to ``sqrt(power)`` around
``delay``, with the steepness of the transition controlled by ``rise``.
Suitable for transient simulations of optical pulse propagation.

Args:
    signals: Port fields and source-current state ``i_src``.
    t: Current simulation time in seconds.
    power: Peak output optical power in watts. Defaults to ``1.0``.
    phase: Output field phase in radians. Defaults to ``0.0``.
    delay: Turn-on delay in seconds. Defaults to ``0.2e-9``.
    rise: Sigmoid rise time constant in seconds. Defaults to ``0.05e-9``.

Prescribed sigmoid optical voltage pulse. Connect p1/p2. This is a voltage clamp, rather than a matched
incident-power source under reflection.

### `OpticalWaveguide`

Single-mode waveguide with first-order dispersion and propagation loss.

The effective index is linearised around ``center_wavelength_nm`` using the
group index to approximate dispersion. Phase and loss are combined into a
complex transmission coefficient ``T``, from which the 2×2 S-matrix and
corresponding exact wave constraints are derived. This is a static
carrier response with no envelope group delay, even though ``n_group``
sets the wavelength dispersion slope.

Args:
    signals: Field amplitudes at input (``p1``) and output (``p2``).
    length_um: Waveguide length in micrometres. Defaults to ``100.0``.
    loss_dB_cm: Propagation loss in dB/cm. Defaults to ``1.0``.
    neff: Effective refractive index at ``center_wavelength_nm``. Defaults to ``2.4``.
    n_group: Group refractive index, used to compute the dispersion slope. Defaults to ``4.0``.
    center_wavelength_nm: Reference wavelength for dispersion expansion in nm. Defaults to ``1310.0``.
    wavelength_nm: Operating wavelength in nm. Defaults to ``1310.0``.

Carrier phase and attenuation for a fixed wavelength.

[Detailed model reference](optical_passive.md) · [API and source](../references/components/photonic.md#circulax.components.photonic.OpticalWaveguide)

### `delay_line_fdomain`

Frequency-domain delay line for AC and harmonic-balance analysis.

Models a pure transmission-line group delay: ``S21 = T_mag * exp(-j 2pi f tau)``
where ``tau = length_um * n_group / c`` and ``T_mag`` accounts for
propagation loss.  The S-matrix is converted to a Y-matrix via
:func:`s_to_y`.

This is a frequency-domain-only component (``f`` = modulation / signal
frequency, e.g. 1 GHz for an AC sweep).  Carrier-phase effects
(``neff``, ``wavelength_nm``) belong in the wavelength-domain
:func:`OpticalWaveguide` and are intentionally excluded here.

This component is AC/HB-only; it cannot be used in transient simulation
(fdomain components raise at transient setup time).

Args:
    f: Modulation frequency in Hz (supplied by the AC/HB solver).
    length_um: Waveguide length in micrometres. Defaults to ``100.0``.
    loss_dB_cm: Propagation loss in dB/cm. Defaults to ``1.0``.
    n_group: Group refractive index; sets the propagation delay via
        ``tau = length_um * n_group / c``. Defaults to ``4.0``.

A frequency-domain delay response.

[Detailed model reference](photonic_conventions.md) · [API and source](../references/components/photonic.md#circulax.components.photonic.delay_line_fdomain)

```python
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np

from circulax.components.photonic import delay_line_fdomain

model = delay_line_fdomain(length_um=100.0)
admittance = model.solver_call(jnp.asarray(1e9), model)
assert admittance.shape == (2, 2)
assert np.isfinite(admittance).all()
```

## Photonic / Passive routing and phase

### `DirectionalCoupler`

4-port directional coupler (2×2 beamsplitter) with configurable power split ratio.

Ports p1/p2 are the input ports; p3/p4 are the output ports.
Signal entering p1 exits at p3 (bar, amplitude t) and p4 (cross, amplitude jk).
Signal entering p2 exits at p3 (cross, jk) and p4 (bar, t).

S-matrix::

    S = [[0, 0, t, jk], [0, 0, jk, t], [t, jk, 0, 0], [jk, t, 0, 0]]

where t = sqrt(1 - coupling), k = sqrt(coupling).

Exact wave constraints support coupling=0 and coupling=1 without loss
or clipping. The full S matrix is reciprocal and unitary for 0<=coupling<=1.
Parameter derivatives of sqrt(coupling) are singular at the endpoints;
use an angle parameterization when differentiating exactly there.

Args:
    signals: Field amplitudes at all four ports.
    coupling: Power fraction routed to the cross port (p4 for p1 input, p3 for p2 input).
        Defaults to ``0.5`` (50/50 splitter).

Four-port coherent power splitting and recombination.

[Detailed model reference](optical_passive.md) · [API and source](../references/components/photonic.md#circulax.components.photonic.DirectionalCoupler)

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np

from circulax.components.photonic import DirectionalCoupler

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
model = DirectionalCoupler()
# Constitutive F/Q evaluation; physical circuit boundaries are shown in the model reference.
y = jnp.zeros(len(model.ports) + len(model.states), dtype=jnp.complex128)
f, q = model.solver_call(0.0, y, model)
assert np.isfinite(f).all()
assert np.isfinite(q).all()
print(DirectionalCoupler.__name__, "ports:", model.ports)
```

    center_wavelength_nm: Peak transmission wavelength in nm. Defaults to ``1310.0``.
    peak_loss_dB: Insertion loss at peak wavelength in dB. Defaults to ``0.0``.
    bandwidth_1dB: Full 1 dB bandwidth in nm. Defaults to ``20.0``.

### `OpticalInterface`

Reciprocal partially reflecting interface with coherent reflection phases.

S=exp(i phase)*10**(-loss_dB/20)*[[sqrt(R)*exp(i delta), sqrt(1-R)],
[sqrt(1-R), -sqrt(R)*exp(-i delta)]]. This is unitary before uniform
loss for 0<=R<=1; the opposite reflection phases are essential for power
conservation under simultaneous excitation. delta=reflection_phase radians.
Full transmission/reflection endpoints are exact; no hidden leakage is added.

Reciprocal partial reflector with coherent phases. Connect p1/p2; exact full transmission and reflection
endpoints are supported.

### `Splitter`

Reciprocal matched three-port splitter with configurable power split.

The full S matrix is contractive, not unitary: its singular values are
(1, 1, 0). A coherent dark combination incident at p2/p3 is absorbed.
A matched reciprocal lossless three-port is impossible. A single input
at p1 divides power without loss. Wave constraints retain exact endpoints.

Args:
    signals: Field amplitudes at the input (``p1``) and two output ports
        (``p2``, ``p3``).
    split_ratio: Fraction of input power routed to ``p2``. The remaining
        ``1 - split_ratio`` is routed to ``p3``. Defaults to ``0.5``
        (50/50 splitter).

The existing passive three-port routing matrix.

### `TunableBeamSplitter`

Directed buffered 2×2 field mixer with a variable coupling angle.

This unilateral behavioral block is not a reciprocal passive scattering
device under arbitrary terminations. For that use DirectionalCoupler.
Implements a tunable beam splitter using a Modified Nodal Analysis (MNA)
voltage-controlled voltage source (VCVS) stamp, which avoids the
near-singular ``(I + S)`` matrix that arises when applying ``s_to_y`` to
a lossless transmission-only S-matrix.

The transmission relations enforced are::

    E_p3 = cos(theta) * E_p1 + j * sin(theta) * E_p2
    E_p4 = j * sin(theta) * E_p1 + cos(theta) * E_p2

Special cases:

* ``theta = 0``       — bar state: ``p1 → p3``, ``p2 → p4`` (no coupling).
* ``theta = pi/4``    — 50/50 beamsplitter (default).
* ``theta = pi/2``    — cross state: ``p1 → p4``, ``p2 → p3`` (full coupling).

Two internal state variables ``i_top`` and ``i_bot`` carry the branch
currents at the output ports ``p3`` and ``p4`` respectively.  The input
ports ``p1`` and ``p2`` contribute no self-stamp; they must be driven by
connected sources or loads to avoid floating nodes.

Gradient flow is exact via ``jax.grad`` for all values of ``theta``
when using the ``"dense"`` solver backend.

Args:
    signals: Port fields and branch-current states ``i_top`` and ``i_bot``.
    theta: Coupling angle in radians.  Controls the power split ratio:
        ``P_cross / P_total = sin²(theta)``.  Defaults to ``pi/4`` (50/50).

Retained directed mixing/combining blocks from older demonstrations.

[Detailed model reference](modulators.md) · [API and source](../references/components/photonic.md#circulax.components.photonic.TunableBeamSplitter)

### `AddDropRing`

Reciprocal four-port ring with independent forward/reverse cavity states.

Bus pairs are p1/p2 and p3/p4; excitation p1 exits through p2 and drops p4.
Couplings gamma_1/gamma_2 and intrinsic gamma_i are amplitude rates 1/s.
detuning=omega_res-omega_ref. Optical waves sqrt(W), cavity states sqrt(J).
Zero couplings are exact; total amplitude rate must remain positive.

A single resonance coupled to two buses.

### `AllPassRing`

Reciprocal matched two-port single-resonance cavity.

gamma_i/gamma_e are amplitude decay rates in 1/s (nonnegative, sum>0).
detuning=2*pi*(f_res-f_ref) in rad/s, carrier convention exp(+i omega_ref t).
c_forward/c_reverse have units sqrt(J). Energy decays at twice amplitude rate.
Through H(s)=1-2*gamma_e/(s+gamma_i+gamma_e-i*detuning).
Valid within one resonance's narrowband CMT region, not multiple FSRs.

A single resonance coupled to one bus, with intrinsic loss and independent counterpropagating modes.

### `OpticalFilter`

Matched low-pass/Lorentzian H(s)=transmission*k/(s+k-i*detuning).

k=2*pi*bandwidth_hz; bandwidth_hz>0 is intensity half-width at half maximum
around envelope frequency detuning/(2*pi). transmission is real amplitude
in [0,1]; z0>0. Cavity-like states c1/c2 store sqrt(J), with dc scaling
b2=sqrt(k)*transmission*c1. Internal dissipation yields a contractive S.
This is a generic single-pole envelope filter, not a broadband resonator.

A matched, reciprocal, causal one-pole Lorentzian envelope filter.

[Detailed model reference](optical_filters.md) · [API and source](../references/components/optical_filters.md#circulax.components.optical_filters.OpticalFilter)

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from circulax import attach_testbench, compile_circuit, quadrature_response
from circulax.components import OpticalCW, OpticalFilter
from circulax.components.electronic import Resistor

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
net = {
    "instances": {"FILTER": {"component": "filter", "settings": {"bandwidth_hz": 1e9}}},
    "ports": {"in": "FILTER,p1", "out": "FILTER,p2"},
}
net = attach_testbench(
    net,
    sources={"in": {"name": "LIGHT", "component": "light", "settings": {"power": 1e-3}}},
    loads={"out": {"name": "LOAD", "component": "resistor", "settings": {"R": 1.0}}},
)
circuit = compile_circuit(net, {"filter": OpticalFilter, "light": OpticalCW, "resistor": Resistor}, is_complex=True)
frequencies = jnp.geomspace(1e7, 1e10, 40)
response = quadrature_response(circuit, freqs=frequencies, parameter_drives={"LIGHT.power": 2 * np.sqrt(1e-3)})
index = circuit.port_map["out"]
transfer = np.asarray(response["in_phase"][:, index] + 1j * response["quadrature"][:, index])
np.testing.assert_allclose(transfer, 1 / (1 + 1j * np.asarray(frequencies) / 1e9), atol=1e-9)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3))
ax.semilogx(np.asarray(frequencies) / 1e9, 20 * np.log10(abs(transfer)))
ax.set(xlabel="Envelope frequency (GHz)", ylabel="Transmission (dB)", title="Native optical filter")
ax.grid(True)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.close(fig)
```

### `RingModulator`

Optical ring modulator via Temporal Coupled-Mode Theory (t-CMT).

Tracks the complex ring energy amplitude ``a(t)`` as an internal state and
enforces the output field relation ``E_o = E_i - j sqrt(2/tau_e) a`` via an
algebraic constraint state ``i_out``.

The ring energy ODE is expressed in the circulax DAE form F + dQ/dt = 0:

- F["a"] = -(da/dt RHS) = j sqrt(2/tau_e) V_p1 - j Delta_omega a + a/tau
- Q["a"] = a

Gives: da/dt = -j sqrt(2/tau_e) E_i + j Delta_omega a - a/tau.

Port ``p1`` contributes zero current (S11 = 0 approximation).
Port ``p2`` is driven by ``i_out`` which enforces the output field.

Args:
    signals: Complex field amplitudes at input (``p1``) and output (``p2``).
    s: Internal states: ``a`` (complex ring energy) and ``i_out`` (output
        constraint current).
    ng: Group refractive index. Defaults to ``3.8``.
    L: Ring circumference in metres. Defaults to ``2*pi*5e-6``.
    gamma: Through-coupling amplitude coefficient. Defaults to ``0.976``.
    alpha0: Voltage-independent round-trip amplitude. Defaults to ``0.969``.
    alpha1: Linear voltage coefficient of round-trip amplitude (1/V).
        Defaults to ``0.0``.
    voltage: Applied DC bias voltage. Defaults to ``0.0``.
    f_operating: Laser frequency in Hz. Defaults to ``2.2904e14``.
    f_resonance: Ring resonance frequency in Hz. Defaults to ``2.2901e14``.
    v_to_wr: Electro-optic coefficient mapping voltage to resonance shift
        in rad/s/V. Defaults to ``0.0``.

Promoted illustrative models preserving older ring notebook behavior.

[Detailed model reference](resonators.md) · [API and source](../references/components/resonators.md#circulax.components.resonators.RingModulator)

### `RingModulatorEO`

Ring modulator with an external electrical voltage port ``v_e``.

The voltage at port ``v_e`` modulates the ring resonance frequency via
``v_to_wr`` (rad/s/V).  The port is high-impedance: it draws no current
(``F["v_e"] = 0``), so any driver circuit sees an open circuit.

The physics is otherwise identical to :func:`RingModulator`, but ``voltage``
is read from the external port rather than being a fixed parameter.

Promoted illustrative models preserving older ring notebook behavior.
